notes: 11,723 loops against 34,474 narrowPeak peaks, of which 6,379 match. The matched file is byte identical, which means three things agree exactly: bedtools' sort order including the permutation of the 3,730 rows that share a start coordinate, pandas' precise_xstrtod float parser (the score 0.0019430592210407135 in the input becomes 0.0019430592210407 in the output because that parser keeps 17 significant digits and then scales, unlike strtod), and repr() of the resulting double.
The other prefix option and the broadPeak reader, which has nine columns of which three are used. str.lstrip('chr') is a character set strip, not a prefix strip, and the port reproduces that.

The many-contig stress case named in PLAN.md 8.1: 313,762 bins over 93 contigs with only 7,987 stored pixels. 11,723 cooler region fetches, each of which parses two region strings, maps them onto bin extents and asks whether the symmetric-upper block holds a pixel. It also exercises cooler's failure paths, which the Python swallows as a non-match: a chromosome the cooler does not have, and a coordinate past the end of a chromosome.

The TAD branch, which writes the matched rows to the bare --outFileName rather than to <name>_matched_locations as the option's help text says, and whose statistics file still calls them Loops. Both reproduced. applyBinning runs with pMerge=False here, so the mask is computed on the de-duplicated binned frame and applied to the unbinned one.

--chrPrefixProtein add was never exercised by the Python suite. Both files already carry a chr prefix, so adding one to each gives chrchr1 on both sides of the comparison but the loops and the peaks still fail to meet, because the loops are prefixed twice and the peaks once more than they were. Nothing matches, the matched file is written and empty, and the ratio prints as 0.0. That last detail is why the case is here: an empty output file is still a file, and the ratio is a float division that must not be printed as an integer.
--outFileName is optional and no test ran without it. Nothing is written and the tool exits 0; the four counts go to stdout only.
